Repo: C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Windows paths, PowerShell/Git-Bash environment). This is Kodely, an AI website builder. No new npm dependencies are allowed.

CONTEXT — read these two files completely before writing anything, they are the exact pattern to generalize:
- lib/site-forms.ts — the ENTIRE safety model for a generated site posting data back to Kodely: same-origin-only POST (`form-action 'self'` in the CSP, see app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts's SANDBOX_CSP constant — do NOT touch that CSP string, this whole feature is designed to need zero CSP changes), origin-header check, body-size caps, field validation, a 3-layer rate limiter (in-process burst + per-IP durable + per-project durable), a honeypot/timing spam check, and HTML (not JSON) responses since a form POST is a navigation.
- app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts — how `POST /__forms/<name>` on `<slug>.kodely.site` gets proxied into this exact Next.js route (see proxy.ts reference in comments) and dispatched to submitSiteForm(). Also note: `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` — published sites are served fresh per request from the database (db.projectFile), not as frozen static snapshots, which is why this whole approach works without any client-side JS.
- prisma/schema.prisma — find the existing `FormSubmission` model and the `Project` model, to match their exact conventions (field naming, indexes, cascade behavior).
- app/projects/[id]/submissions/ (or wherever the owner currently views form submissions in the authenticated dashboard — find it) — the pattern for how a project owner sees data their site collected. This is your template for the new owner-facing view.

THE GOAL: build "Phase 0" of a larger plan to let generated sites have real, safe backend-backed features (bookings, client portals, simple data) later, WITHOUT ever letting the AI write or run arbitrary server code. Phase 0 is just the generic storage/write/view foundation — no booking-specific or CRUD-specific product logic yet, that's future work. Do not build anything beyond what's listed below; this must stay a clean, reusable primitive.

BUILD:

1. A new Prisma model, `SiteRecord`, generalizing `FormSubmission`:
   - `id` (cuid), `projectId` (FK to Project, cascade delete — copy FormSubmission's exact relation style), `kind` (String — like `formName` on FormSubmission, a short identifier like "booking" or "listing"), `fields` (Json — the record's own payload, same shape discipline as FormSubmission.fields: validated key names, capped sizes), `status` (String, default "active" — lets a record be superseded/cancelled without deleting history), `ipHash` (String, same salted-hash approach as FormSubmission.ipHash, for rate limiting), `spam` (Boolean, default false, same honeypot-flag pattern as FormSubmission), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`.
   - Add an index on `(projectId, kind, createdAt)` for the owner's list view and the per-project rate-limit queries.
   - Do NOT run any Prisma migration or `prisma db push` yourself — write the schema change, then tell me in your final report the exact command to run (e.g. `npx prisma migrate dev --name add_site_record`) so I can review and run it myself.

2. A new `lib/site-records.ts`, mirroring lib/site-forms.ts's complete safety machinery:
   - Same same-origin-only enforcement (host check via siteHostAllowed, origin-header check).
   - Same body-size caps, field-name/value validation, honeypot + timing spam check.
   - Same 3-layer rate limiting (in-process burst, per-IP durable, per-project durable) — reuse the exact same constants/approach, adjusted only if a genuinely different limit makes sense for records vs. forms (state your reasoning if you change any number).
   - Where the logic is IDENTICAL to site-forms.ts (host/origin checks, body reading, rate-limit bucket math), factor it into a small shared helper both files import, rather than copy-pasting verbatim — but don't over-abstract; only extract what is genuinely identical.
   - The endpoint shape: `POST /__records/<kind>` (parallel to the existing `/__forms/<name>`), same plain `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` handling, same HTML-response-not-JSON pattern (it's a navigation, not a fetch).
   - `kind` must be validated against a short allow-list style pattern (same regex discipline as FORM_NAME_RE) — reject anything not matching, same as an unknown form name 404s today.
   - Store the parsed fields as `SiteRecord.fields`, exactly the safety discipline FormSubmission.fields already has (validated key names, capped value lengths, control fields like `_gotcha`/`_t`/`_next` handled identically to site-forms.ts).
   - No email notification needed for this generic path (that's form-specific) — just the safe write.

3. Wire `POST /__records/<kind>` into app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts's existing POST handler, parallel to how `/__forms/<name>` already dispatches to submitSiteForm — read the path segments and dispatch to your new site-records.ts handler when the first segment is `__records` instead of `__forms`.

4. A real, authenticated owner-facing view: find and read the existing form-submissions view pattern (likely under app/projects/[id]/) and build an equivalent page (or extend that same page with a kind filter/tab, whichever fits the existing UI pattern better — use your judgment after reading it) so a project owner can see the SiteRecords their published site has collected, grouped or filterable by `kind`. Follow this project's existing design system (docs/design-system.md, existing Card/Badge/EmptyState components under components/ui/) rather than inventing new UI patterns.

5. Do NOT add any CSP relaxation anywhere. Do NOT add any client-side fetch/XHR capability to generated sites. Do NOT build booking-specific conflict-checking logic, availability calendars, or any other product feature on top of this — this task is the storage/write/view foundation ONLY.

6. Run `cd /c/Users/edmem/kodely-prod && npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0` — both must be completely clean before you finish. (tsc will likely need the Prisma client regenerated after your schema edit — run `npx prisma generate` if needed, that's safe and non-destructive, just don't run migrate/db push.)

Report back: the exact Prisma migration command I need to run, a summary of what you built in site-records.ts and how it shares logic with site-forms.ts, where the new owner-facing view lives, and confirmation both checks passed clean.

33	// requests" contract had a hole big enough to walk a phishing form through:
34	// `connect-src 'none'` stops fetch/XHR and stops nothing else, so
35	// `<form action="https://attacker.example">` submitted cross-origin and
36	// carried whatever a visitor typed.
37	//
38	//   form-action 'self' — the only POST a generated page may make is to its own
39	//     origin. Everything else — <form action="https://attacker.example">,
40	//     formaction= on a button — is refused by the browser before a byte leaves.
41	//     Contact CTAs of the tel:/mailto:/sms: kind are <a href> and form-action
42	//     does not touch them either way.
43	//
44	//     UNCHANGED BY FORM SUBMISSIONS, and that is the point. Generated sites can
45	//     now have working contact forms (lib/site-forms.ts, POST below), and this
46	//     directive did NOT have to be widened by a single character to allow it,
47	//     because `'self'` is the SITE's origin — https://<slug>.kodely.site — and
48	//     that origin is already us: proxy.ts rewrites every request on it into
49	//     this very route. So a form whose action is `/__forms/<name>` is a
50	//     same-origin POST that lands in the same handler that served the page.
51	//     Pointing the form at kodely.me instead would have been cross-origin and
52	//     would have meant adding an external origin to form-action on every
53	//     customer site on the platform — a real loosening, for nothing.
54	//
55	//     Note what is still refused: a page may POST to its own origin and to
56	//     nowhere else, and only the paths this route answers do anything. The
57	//     phishing shape this directive was added for (a generated page collecting
58	//     what a visitor types and shipping it to an attacker) is exactly as
59	//     impossible as it was before.
60	//
61	//     `connect-src 'none'` is untouched and must stay that way. A form POST is
62	//     a navigation, not a scripted request, so nothing here needs it — which is
63	//     also why the submission endpoint answers with HTML rather than JSON.
64	//   base-uri 'none' — an injected <base href> would silently repoint every
65	//     relative URL on the page, which is a way to smuggle a remote origin back
66	//     in past the directives above.
67	//   object-src 'none' — plugin content has no use on a static generated page,
68	//     and it does not fall back to default-src either.
69	//
70	// MUST STAY IN SYNC with the copy in app/api/preview/[id]/[[...path]]/route.ts,
71	// which serves the same generated markup to the editor's iframe. It is a
72	// separate constant in a separate file on purpose (that route is owner-only
73	// and has its own MIME table); there is no shared module for the two.
74	const SANDBOX_CSP =
75	  "default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'";
76	
77	/**
78	 * Which stored build file answers a requested URL path.
79	 *
80	 * Generated sites are multi-page (lib/foundation.ts): `vite build` emits a real
81	 * document per page — index.html, about.html, blog/index.html — and visitors
82	 * ask for /about, not /about.html. This is the whole server-side cost of that.
83	 *
84	 * Deliberately NOT the SPA catch-all ("serve index.html for anything unknown").
85	 * That shape is what a client-side router needs, and it turns every typo, every
86	 * dead inbound link and every stale crawl URL into a 200 serving the home page —
87	 * soft 404s, which Google treats as a quality problem on the whole site. Here a
88	 * path resolves only to a file that actually exists under one of two well-known
89	 * spellings, and everything else still 404s exactly as it did before.
90	 *
91	 * Anything carrying an extension resolves to itself and nothing else, which is
92	 * what keeps robots.txt, sitemap.xml and /assets/* on their existing single
93	 * path — no candidate list can shadow them.
94	 */
95	function candidatePaths(filePath: string): string[] {
96	  if (/\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$/.test(filePath)) return [filePath];
97	  const clean = filePath.replace(/\/+$/, "");
98	  if (!clean) return ["index.html"];
99	  // Order matters: about.html wins over about/index.html when a site has both.
100	  return [`${clean}.html`, `${clean}/index.html`];
101	}
102	
103	/**
104	 * Form submissions from a published site: `POST /__forms/<formName>`, which
105	 * arrives here as `/api/site/<slug>/__forms/<formName>` via proxy.ts.
106	 *
107	 * Everything — host check, published check, caps, abuse control, storage and
108	 * the owner notification — is in lib/site-forms.ts. Anything that is not that
109	 * exact path shape is a 404 there, so this does not become a general POST
110	 * surface on the sites domain.
111	 */
112	export async function POST(
113	  req: Request,
114	  { params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string; path?: string[] }> },
115	) {
116	  const { slug, path } = await params;
117	  return submitSiteForm(req, slug, path ?? []);
118	}
119	
120	export async function GET(
121	  req: Request,
122	  { params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string; path?: string[] }> },
123	) {
124	  const { slug, path } = await params;
125	  const filePath = path && path.length > 0 ? path.join("/") : "index.html";
126	
127	  // Generated pages are only ever first-party to the sites domain. proxy.ts
128	  // turns this request away earlier for the same reason, but a route handler
129	  // must not depend on that: the proxy's own matcher can miss paths, and the
130	  // proxy is explicit (see its header comment) that it is never the only gate.
131	  //
132	  // The response is byte-identical to the "no such site" 404 below, so it does
133	  // not confirm that a slug exists to someone probing the wrong host.
134	  if (!siteHostAllowed(req.headers.get("host") ?? "", slug)) {
135	    return new Response("Site not found.", { status: 404 });
136	  }
137	
138	  const project = await db.project.findUnique({ where: { slug } });
139	  if (!project || !project.publishedAt) {
140	    return new Response("Site not found.", { status: 404 });
141	  }
142	
143	  const baseUrl = siteBaseUrl(req, slug);
144	  const seoHeaders = {
145	    "Content-Security-Policy": SANDBOX_CSP,
146	    "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=60",
147	  };
148	
149	  // robots.txt and sitemap.xml are generated, not stored — they depend on the
150	  // visitor-facing host (which differs between the branded subdomain and the
151	  // staging path form), so a file baked at build time would be wrong on one of
152	  // them. A site that ships its own copy still wins: we only synthesise these
153	  // when the project has no such file.
154	  if (filePath === "robots.txt" || filePath === "sitemap.xml") {
155	    const own = await db.projectFile.findFirst({
156	      where: { projectId: project.id, path: filePath, published: true, kind: "build" },
157	    });
158	    if (!own) {
159	      if (filePath === "robots.txt") {
160	        return new Response(robotsTxt(baseUrl), {
161	          headers: { ...seoHeaders, "Content-Type": MIME.txt },
162	        });
163	      }
164	      const pages = await db.projectFile.findMany({
165	        where: { projectId: project.id, published: true, kind: "build", path: { endsWith: ".html" } },
166	        select: { path: true },
167	      });
168	      return new Response(
169	        sitemapXml(baseUrl, pages.map((p) => p.path), project.publishedAt ?? undefined),
170	        { headers: { ...seoHeaders, "Content-Type": MIME.xml } },
171	      );
172	    }
173	  }
174	
175	  // One query for both spellings of a page, then the caller's preference order
176	  // decides — /about must not cost two round trips to answer.
177	  const candidates = candidatePaths(filePath);
178	  const matches = await db.projectFile.findMany({
179	    where: { projectId: project.id, path: { in: candidates }, published: true, kind: "build" },
180	  });
181	  const file = candidates.map((c) => matches.find((m) => m.path === c)).find(Boolean);
182	  if (!file) {
183	    return new Response("Not found.", { status: 404 });
184	  }
185	
186	  const ext = file.path.split(".").pop() ?? "";
187	
188	  // Backstop so no site can ship with the foundation's placeholder <title>.
189	  // Only fills gaps — anything the builder wrote itself is preserved.
190	  //
191	  // pageUrl(), not baseUrl: canonical and og:url must name THIS page. Keyed off
192	  // the file that actually answered, so /about and /about.html both canonicalise
193	  // to /about and Google sees one page rather than two competing duplicates.
194	  const body =
195	    ext === "html"
196	      ? applySeo(file.content, {
197	          projectName: project.name,
198	          baseUrl,
199	          pageUrl: pageUrl(baseUrl, file.path),
200	        })
201	      : file.content;
202	
203	  return new Response(body, {
204	    headers: { ...seoHeaders, "Content-Type": MIME[ext] ?? "application/octet-stream" },
205	  });
206	}

1	// Kodely — Phase 1 data model.
2	// Principles baked in here (see the Kodely board):
3	//  - every generation is a Build row with real token counts, so cost per build is never a guess
4	//  - credits are a ledger, never a mutable counter: the balance is derivable and auditable
5	//  - failed builds are recorded but NEVER charged
6	
7	generator client {
8	  provider = "prisma-client-js"
9	}
10	
11	datasource db {
12	  provider = "postgresql"
13	  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
14	}
15	
16	model User {
17	  id               String   @id @default(cuid())
18	  email            String   @unique
19	  // Nullable because a Google-only account never sets a local password.
20	  passwordHash     String?
21	  googleId         String?  @unique
22	  name             String?
23	  role             String   @default("CUSTOMER") // CUSTOMER | ADMIN
24	  stripeCustomerId String?
25	  createdAt        DateTime @default(now())
26	
27	  // Self-imposed ceiling on credits spent per rolling 30 days. NULL = no cap.
28	  // This is the user's own guard against a runaway session, not a plan limit —
29	  // bill shock is the category's deepest trust wound (one competitor billed
30	  // $607 against a $25 plan in three days), and a cap the user sets themselves
31	  // is the cheapest honest answer to it.
32	  spendCapCredits Int?
33	
34	  // Set when the user asks for erasure, cleared if they cancel. The grace
35	  // period is measured from here.
36	  //
37	  // Exists because the alternative was worse: the request was being recorded as
38	  // marker-prefixed SupportNote rows, which then appeared in an operator-notes
39	  // UI that describes itself as "operator-written, never customer-facing" — one
40	  // of those rows was neither. A lifecycle fact belongs on the user, not
41	  // smuggled into a table meant for something else.
42	  deletionRequestedAt DateTime?
43	
44	  // ── Nxeon (domains / VPS / shared hosting), all optional ──────────────────
45	  //
46	  // @unique because two Kodely accounts silently sharing one Nxeon identity
47	  // is a support incident waiting to happen (whose wallet, whose server?) —
48	  // the callback treats a collision as a hard error, never a second link.
49	  //
50	  // Deliberately flat fields rather than a child table: Nxeon provisions AT
51	  // MOST one of each product per Kodely account today (the checkout call
52	  // carries no slot/index), so a one-row-per-user shape cannot under- or
53	  // over-count. Revisit as a table only if Nxeon ever lets one account hold
54	  // more than one server, domain or hosting account.
55	  //
56	  // IMPORTANT — what this does NOT do: buying a domain here does not point it
57	  // at a Kodely site, and provisioning a VPS/hosting account here does not
58	  // deploy the Kodely-built site onto it. Nxeon's API (see lib/nxeon.ts)
59	  // covers identity linking, checkout and provisioning notification only —
60	  // actually shipping generated files onto Nxeon infrastructure is unbuilt
61	  // and is a separate piece of work.
62	  nxeonUserId String? @unique
63	
64	  nxeonServerId       String?
65	  nxeonServerIp       String?
66	  nxeonServerHostname String?
67	
68	  nxeonDomain          String?
69	  nxeonDomainExpiresAt DateTime?
70	
71	  nxeonHostingAccountId String?
72	  nxeonHostingDomain    String?
73	
74	  sessions     Session[]
75	  projects     Project[]
76	  ledger       CreditLedger[]
77	  events       Event[]
78	  supportNotes SupportNote[]
79	  supportTickets SupportTicket[]
80	}
81	
82	// Idempotency guard for Nxeon's webhook, same shape and same reason as
83	// StripeEvent: `id` is the primary key, so a retried or duplicated delivery
84	// hits a P2002 conflict and is skipped rather than applied twice. An HMAC
85	// signature proves the request came from Nxeon; it says nothing about whether
86	// we have already handled this exact delivery.
87	model NxeonEvent {
88	  id        String   @id
89	  type      String
90	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
91	}
92	
93	// First-party analytics. Self-hosted deliberately: cheaper, keeps the data
94	// ours, avoids another paid API on the critical path, and is privacy-clean.
95	//
96	// One wide table rather than a table per dashboard, because the activation
97	// funnel, retention cohorts, per-user journey, attribution and the overview
98	// tiles are all different queries over the same stream. Build it once, or
99	// every dashboard invents its own tracking.
100	model Event {
101	  id     String  @id @default(cuid())
102	  // Nullable so pre-signup events (landing view, prompt submitted) still land.
103	  userId String?
104	  /// Dotted, past-tense name — see EVENTS in lib/events.ts. Never free text.
105	  name   String
106	  /// Small, non-PII payload: ids, counts, enum-ish strings. Never prompt bodies.
107	  props  Json?
108	
109	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
110	
111	  user User? @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
112	
113	  // Funnels scan by name over a window; journeys scan one user over a window.
114	  @@index([name, createdAt])
115	  @@index([userId, createdAt])
116	}
117	
118	// A submission from a form on a PUBLISHED generated site.
119	//
120	// This is the one deliberate hole in "generated sites have no backend", and it
121	// exists because the alternative is worse: the builder is currently forbidden
122	// from drawing a contact form at all, because a form that silently discards a
123	// real enquiry is worse than no form — and a live blog post already told dental
124	// practices their appointment requests were arriving when they were not.
125	//
126	// Submissions land HERE, on Kodely's origin, never on the customer's site. The
127	// generated page stays static; only the POST target is ours.
128	model FormSubmission {
129	  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
130	  projectId String
131	  /// Which form on the page, when a site has more than one.
132	  formName  String   @default("contact")
133	  /// The submitted fields. Untrusted public input — never rendered as HTML,
134	  /// never interpolated into a query, and capped hard at write time.
135	  fields    Json
136	  /// For rate limiting and abuse triage only. Not shown to the site owner.
137	  ipHash    String?
138	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
139	
140	  readAt DateTime?
141	  /// Set when it looks like spam. Kept rather than dropped, so a false
142	  /// positive is recoverable and the rate is measurable.
143	  spam   Boolean @default(false)
144	
145	  project Project @relation(fields: [projectId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
146	
147	  @@index([projectId, createdAt])
148	  @@index([createdAt])
149	}
150	
151	// Pre-auth attempt counter for login and signup.
152	//
153	// Exists because the limiter that guards them cannot key on a user id — there
154	// is no session yet — and every other limiter in lib/rate-limit.ts counts rows
155	// the feature already writes (Build, Project). A failed login writes nothing,
156	// so without this table the counter can only live in process memory, where it
157	// resets on every deploy and multiplies by the process count.
158	//
159	// `key` is the bucket, already hashed by the caller: an IP, or a salted digest
160	// of an email. Deliberately never the plaintext address — this table would
161	// otherwise become a running list of every address anyone tried to log in as,
162	// which is a worse thing to hold than the problem it solves.
163	model LoginAttempt {
164	  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
165	  key       String
166	  /// "ip" | "account" | "signup" — so one table serves every pre-auth bucket
167	  /// without the scopes colliding on a shared key.
168	  scope     String
169	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
170	
171	  // The only query shape: count rows for one bucket inside a window, and prune
172	  // everything older. Both are served by this index.
173	  @@index([scope, key, createdAt])
174	  @@index([createdAt])
175	}
176	
177	// One row per transactional email actually sent.
178	//
179	// Without this, notification idempotency has to be derived from a time window,
180	// which is at-most-once: a skipped cron run drops that window, and a process
181	// restart mid-window can resend. The unique constraint below makes it
182	// exactly-once — the insert IS the claim, so two workers racing produce one
183	// email and one conflict.
184	//
185	// `dedupeKey` is the id of the thing that triggered it (the ledger row that
186	// dropped someone into "low", the failed build, the project first published),
187	// NOT a timestamp. That is what makes the guarantee independent of scheduling.
188	model EmailLog {
189	  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
190	  userId    String
191	  /// welcome | low_credits | build_failed | site_published
192	  kind      String
193	  dedupeKey String
194	  sentAt    DateTime @default(now())
195	
196	  @@unique([kind, dedupeKey])
197	  @@index([userId, sentAt])
198	}
199	
200	// Who did what in the admin panel. Admin surfaces read cost, margin, customer
201	// prompts and personal data; without a log, "who looked at this account" has no
202	// answer. Append-only by convention — nothing in the app updates or deletes a row.
203	model AdminAuditLog {
204	  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
205	  /// The admin who acted. Kept as a plain id, not a relation, so the record
206	  /// survives that admin's account being deleted.
207	  actorId    String
208	  actorEmail String
209	  /// Dotted, past-tense: "user.viewed", "site.taken_down", "flag.changed".
210	  action     String
211	  targetType String?
212	  targetId   String?
213	  /// Small, non-PII context. Never prompt bodies or generated content.
214	  meta       Json?
215	  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())
216	
217	  @@index([actorId, createdAt])
218	  @@index([action, createdAt])
219	  @@index([targetType, targetId])
220	}
221	
222	// Runtime kill switches and gradual rollout. Deliberately a table rather than
223	// env vars: flipping a flag must not require a deploy, which is the entire
224	// point of having a kill switch.
225	model FeatureFlag {
226	  key         String   @id
227	  enabled     Boolean  @default(false)
228	  description String   @default("")
229	  /// 0-100. Ignored when `enabled` is false. Bucketed by user id so a given
230	  /// user's answer is stable rather than flickering between requests.
231	  rolloutPct  Int      @default(100)
232	  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
233	  updatedBy   String?
234	}
235	
236	// One row per moderation finding per publish attempt. Sub-blocking findings
237	// previously went only to console.warn — enough to reconstruct one site after
238	// it is reported, not enough to query proactively, and not enough to ever
239	// measure the false-positive rate that gates promoting a rule to blocking.
240	model ModerationFinding {
241	  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
242	  projectId String
243	  rule      String
244	  severity  String // high | medium | low
245	  path      String
246	  evidence  String
247	  /// "blocked" when this finding stopped the publish, "recorded" otherwise.
248	  action    String
249	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
250	
251	  reviewedAt DateTime?
252	  reviewedBy String?
253	  /// Set on review: "true_positive" | "false_positive".
254	  outcome    String?
255	
256	  @@index([projectId, createdAt])
257	  @@index([severity, createdAt])
258	  @@index([rule, createdAt])
259	}
260	
261	// Operator-written notes about a customer, for support continuity. Never shown
262	// to the customer, so it must never be used to store anything we would not
263	// stand behind if disclosed in a data-subject access request.
264	model SupportNote {
265	  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
266	  userId      String
267	  authorEmail String
268	  body        String
269	  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
270	
271	  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
272	
273	  @@index([userId, createdAt])
274	}
275	
276	// ── Support tickets: a conversation WITH the customer ─────────────────────
277	//
278	// SupportNote (above) and SupportMessage (below) are NOT the same thing and
279	// must never be merged, however similar the columns look:
280	//
281	//   SupportNote     operator prose ABOUT a person. Written by staff, read by
282	//                   staff, NEVER rendered to the customer. It is disclosable
283	//                   in a subject access request — the export returns its body
284	//                   — but disclosure-on-request and publication-in-the-UI are
285	//                   different things, and only the first one applies here.
286	//   SupportMessage  one turn of a conversation WITH a person. Either side may
287	//                   have written it, and EVERY row of it — including the ones
288	//                   staff wrote — is rendered in that customer's own thread on
289	//                   /support the moment it is created.
290	//
291	// So the safety property is: a staff SupportMessage is published to the
292	// customer by construction, and a SupportNote never is. Anything an operator
293	// would only write because the customer cannot see it belongs in a note. If a
294	// note ever needs to become an answer, it has to be re-written as a message on
295	// purpose; nothing in the app copies between the two tables, in either
296	// direction, and nothing should.
297	//
298	// Both are destroyed on erasure (app/api/account/_deletion.ts) and both appear
299	// in the data export.
300	model SupportTicket {
301	  id     String @id @default(cuid())
302	  userId String
303	
304	  /// bug | feature | billing | help. Closed set — SUPPORT_CATEGORIES in
305	  /// lib/support.ts is the contract, and the sidebar's "Bug or idea" menu
306	  /// links straight at two of them via /support?topic=…
307	  category String @default("help")
308	  subject  String
309	
310	  /// OPEN | ANSWERED | RESOLVED. Three, because only three are real: OPEN and
311	  /// ANSWERED are derived from who wrote last (nobody types them), and
312	  /// RESOLVED is the one a human sets. There is deliberately no "pending", no
313	  /// "escalated" and no priority column — nothing measures or acts on any of
314	  /// them, and a status nobody sets is a status that lies.
315	  status String @default("OPEN")
316	
317	  /// Which site this is about, when it is about one. SetNull rather than
318	  /// Cascade: deleting a project must not destroy the ticket that explains why
319	  /// it was deleted, and a thread whose site is gone still reads correctly.
320	  projectId String?
321	
322	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
323	  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
324	
325	  /// When the newest message on the thread landed. The list ORDER, kept
326	  /// separate from `updatedAt` on purpose: `updatedAt` also moves when someone
327	  /// merely opens the thread (the read marks below are updates), and a list
328	  /// that reshuffles because a page was viewed is a list you cannot trust.
329	  lastMessageAt DateTime @default(now())
330	
331	  /// When staff last replied. NULL means nobody has. Denormalised so "is there
332	  /// an unread reply" is answerable for a whole page of tickets without a join
333	  /// per row; written in the same transaction as the message it describes.
334	  lastStaffMessageAt DateTime?
335	
336	  // ── Read state, both sides. Neither is derivable from the other. ──────────
337	  /// When the customer last opened this thread. `lastStaffMessageAt` newer
338	  /// than this is what puts "New reply" on their list.
339	  customerReadAt DateTime?
340	  /// When an operator last opened it. With status OPEN — which is exactly the
341	  /// case where the last message is the customer's — this is what separates
342	  /// "nobody has looked at this yet" from "seen, not yet answered".
343	  staffReadAt DateTime?
344	
345	  user     User             @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
346	  project  Project?         @relation(fields: [projectId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
347	  messages SupportMessage[]
348	
349	  // The customer's own list, the admin's status filter, and the admin's
350	  // unfiltered list. All three sort by lastMessageAt desc.
351	  @@index([userId, lastMessageAt])
352	  @@index([status, lastMessageAt])
353	  @@index([lastMessageAt])
354	}
355	
356	model SupportMessage {
357	  id       String @id @default(cuid())
358	  ticketId String
359	
360	  /// CUSTOMER | STAFF. A string rather than a boolean because "isStaff: false"
361	  /// reads as an absence, and the one thing this column must never be is
362	  /// ambiguous — it decides whose name goes on a message the customer reads.
363	  author String

## Report

**Migration command to run:** `npx prisma migrate dev --name add_site_record` (I did not run it or `db push`, per instructions).

### `kind`/`fields` genericity — confirmed
Per the coordinator's clarification mid-task: `kind` is validated only against the URL-safe token regex `PATH_IDENTIFIER_RE` (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$/`, shared with `FORM_NAME_RE`) — there is no enum, allow-list of known kinds, or "booking"/"listing" special-casing anywhere in `lib/site-records.ts`, the schema, or the owner view. `fields` is stored as arbitrary `Json` under the same generic key/value caps `FormSubmission.fields` already used (`MAX_FIELDS`, `MAX_KEY_LENGTH`, `MAX_VALUE_LENGTH`, `FIELD_NAME_RE`) — no field-name assumptions, no shape checks. The owner-facing view (`app/projects/[id]/records/page.tsx`) builds its kind tabs from a `groupBy(["kind"])` query against whatever kinds actually exist for that project, not a hardcoded list. No booking-specific validation or conflict-checking exists anywhere.

### What was built
- **`prisma/schema.prisma`**: new `SiteRecord` model (`id`, `projectId`, `kind`, `fields` Json, `status` default `"active"`, `ipHash`, `spam`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`), `@@index([projectId, kind, createdAt])`, cascade delete from `Project`, plus `Project.records SiteRecord[]`.
- **`lib/site-endpoint.ts`** (new): the machinery genuinely identical between forms and records — host/origin checks (`originAllowed`, `siteBase`), capped body reading (`readCapped`), field parsing (`parseFields`, same caps/regex), IP hashing (`hashIp`, salt passed in per-caller so the two features' hashes are never comparable), a burst-limiter factory (`createBurstLimiter`, each caller gets its own instance/state), honeypot+timing spam check (`isLikelySpam`), the `_next` redirect resolver, and the shared HTML-reply plumbing (`htmlReply`, `escapeHtml`, `siteNotFound`). `lib/site-forms.ts` was refactored to import from this module instead of duplicating it — its behavior/wording/rate-limit numbers are unchanged.
- **`lib/site-records.ts`** (new): mirrors `site-forms.ts`'s safety model for `POST /__records/<kind>` — same origin/host enforcement, same body caps, same field validation, same honeypot/timing check, same three-layer rate limiting (kept identical to forms' numbers — 8/5min burst, 15/hr & 50/day per IP, 60/hr & 300/day per project — since a generic unauthenticated write endpoint has the same abuse profile as forms; noted as such in the file's comments).
